subject.title: Session `status` field values ("failed", "timeout", "done") mislead agents into spawning duplicate sessions

question: Should session rows expose an additive `resumable`/status-semantics signal for `sessions_list`, or should OpenClaw instead rename/split the existing `status` lifecycle contract?
rationale: Both paths change model-visible session semantics, and the prior implementation also raised scope questions around `killed` and the shared Gateway row contract; automation should not choose that permanent API direction alone.

options.title: Add resumability metadata
options.body: Keep existing status values for compatibility and add a clear `resumable` signal plus tool/prompt guidance so agents prefer `sessions_send` where appropriate.

options.title: Rename or split status
options.body: Define a new lifecycle/turn-state contract and migrate callers/tests, accepting the compatibility work required by breaking or parallel status semantics.

options.title: Document only
options.body: Leave the row shape unchanged and document the current status meaning, accepting that model-facing ambiguity may continue.

recommendation.title: Add resumability metadata
recommendation.body: Keep existing status values for compatibility and add a clear `resumable` signal plus tool/prompt guidance so agents prefer `sessions_send` where appropriate.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and authored much of the session status/list history and are the strongest routing candidate for the shared Gateway/agent row contract decision.
